extracted.intended_audience: NIA K99/R00 grant reviewers, NIH program officers, and research mentors/trainees
extracted.subtask_description: A K99/R00 Pathway to Independence career development and research plan for a postdoctoral candidate proposing training, mentorship, and pilot research to develop an intervention and tools for home hospice dementia care and to transition to R01-funded independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective 1: Extend knowledge in core substantive areas (hospice, dementia caregiving, recruitment and retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire deeper knowledge of hospice operations and care delivery, dementia caregiving, and recruitment and retention—particularly for vulnerable, underrepresented groups (e.g., African American persons, hospice patients, persons with dementia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include shadowing clinicians who provide home hospice care, attending grand rounds and team meetings (monthly) and Center meetings (weekly), becoming a trainer in an existing multi-site R33 hospice training program, and attending the USC Roybal scientific training program on health disparities in dementia. Purpose: to learn realities/constraints of clinical settings and design feasible, acceptable, scalable tools compatible with existing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective 2: Develop, implement, and disseminate behavioral interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain expertise in best practices for developing rigorous, robust behavioral interventions for clinical settings, workforce training, goal attainment scaling, and community collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Didactic experiences include coursework and training seminars (e.g., NIH Training Institute on Dissemination & Implementation Research; Johns Hopkins Center for Innovative Care in Aging Behavioral Interventions), mentorship from experts in intervention development, and use of this training to develop a training- and tool-based intervention for home hospice clinicians to support family caregivers of persons with dementia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective 3: Design and conduct clinical trials (RCTs and pragmatic trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the skills to design, implement, and evaluate randomized controlled trials and pragmatic trials in constrained, real-world clinical settings (e.g., home hospice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned training options include applying to NIH Summer Institute on Randomized Behavioral Clinical Trials, completing WCM Clinical Trials Design and Analysis workshops, WCM Protocol Writing Workshop, and NIH Pragmatic and Group-Randomized Trials online course. Engagement with mentors experienced in pragmatic multisite trials is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective 4: Professional development in grant writing and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen grant-writing abilities (especially R-level grants), build collaborative networks for multi-site studies, and obtain professional development training to support transition to independence and competitive R00/R01 applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include Responsible Conduct of Research training, WCM Planning & Writing Successful Grant Proposals workshop, applying for Leadership in Academic Medicine Program, attending work-in-progress sessions, presenting at national conferences (GSA, AAHPM, ASA), and mentor-guided grant preparation with the explicit goal of submitting R00 and later R01 applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship team composition and documented commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble an interdisciplinary mentorship team with documented expertise and commitments to provide guidance, training opportunities, and resources supporting the candidate's learning objectives and proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application should identify primary and co-mentors with relevant records (e.g., Dr. Prigerson as primary mentor with R01s and mentoring experience), specify the distinct contribution of each mentor (e.g., EOL care, dementia caregiving, RCT design), and include letters indicating resource commitments (e.g., provision of statistical, research, administrative support from mentor's grants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship intensity and meeting schedule (K99 vs R00)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline and frequency of mentor interactions showing intensive mentorship during the K99 phase and reduced (but ongoing) mentorship during the R00 phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example schedule: weekly hour-long meetings with primary mentor during K99; monthly meetings with key co-mentors; quarterly meetings with other mentors/advisors in K99; semi-annual or quarterly light-touch meetings during R00. Mentorship should include active involvement in project development, analyses, manuscript and grant preparation, and transition planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to NIA Stage Model for intervention development
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the proposed research to provide Stage 0 (basic science), Stage 1A (intervention development), and Stage 1B (preliminary testing) per the NIA Stage Model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The research plan should explicitly tie activities to Stage 0–1B aims: formative qualitative work, adaptation/development of materials and tools, pilot feasibility/acceptability testing, and preliminary efficacy data to support future R01 trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 1: Identification of common challenges, strategies and gaps (qualitative interview plan and sample)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct semi-structured interviews with stakeholders to identify common caregiving challenges, strategies, and gaps in community-dwelling persons with dementia near end-of-life, including differences by race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned sample: African American FCG (n=20), white FCG (n=20), bereaved FCG, and clinicians (n=20) recruited from VNSNY hospice, WCM practice sites, and community organizations. The aim should address subgroup (African American vs white) differences (Sub-Aim 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 2: Adapt culturally inclusive training materials and develop goal-assessment tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Create dementia-focused training materials tailored to home hospice and a goal-assessment tool that encompasses a culturally inclusive range of challenges, goals, and outcomes and guides clinicians in tailoring care to individual caregiver needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate perspectives of racially diverse stakeholders identified in Aim 1; adapt existing materials to address challenges specific to home hospice; ensure the tool can adapt to personalized needs of family caregivers and supports culturally inclusive practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and acceptability thresholds for clinician training and tool (Aim 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-specify measurable feasibility and acceptability criteria to evaluate the training and tool among home hospice clinicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesized thresholds: >70% of home hospice clinicians will (1) complete the training, (2) report the training and tool are useful, (3) increase knowledge of dementia-related challenges and care strategies, and (4) increase confidence in providing dementia-related care. Use these metrics to decide on revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot efficacy outcomes and exploratory analyses (Aim 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define primary and exploratory outcomes for a pilot test comparing intervention to usual care and plan analyses including examination of disparities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary outcome: reduction in family caregiver (FCG) burden reported by FCG in the intervention group. Exploratory outcomes: lower rates of hospice disenrollment among persons with dementia served by intervention clinicians. Exploratory analyses: examine racial disparities in FCG burden and patient disenrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training activities and didactic experiences (types, timing, and expected completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify concrete didactic experiences (shadowing, short workshops, online courses, multi-day or multi-month programs) and schedule across K99 year(s) to build competency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: clinician shadowing (about 10 days), Hospice Champion Training (2 days), NIH or equivalent training institutes (dissemination & implementation, randomized trials), WCM Protocol Writing Workshop (4 weeks), Clinical Trials workshops (1 day each), NIH Pragmatic and Group-Randomized Trials online course. Provide contingency plans if not accepted to selective programs (attend alternatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and retention competency for vulnerable and underrepresented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop specific skills and strategies for recruiting, enrolling, and retaining vulnerable, hard-to-reach, and underrepresented populations (e.g., hospice patients, persons with dementia, African American caregivers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include mentor-guided training, meeting with community partners, becoming involved in outreach/trainer roles, and using pilot studies to refine recruitment/retention approaches. The career plan should demonstrate how this competency will be applied during the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool design requirement: culturally inclusive, flexible, clinically useful
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal-assessment tool must be culturally inclusive, flexible to personalize across a range of caregiver challenges and goals, and clinically useful to guide home hospice clinicians in suggesting management strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool development should be informed by diverse stakeholder input (Aim 1 & 2), iteratively revised following feasibility/acceptability testing (Aim 3), and designed for integration into routine hospice workflows to facilitate scalability and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and career outputs to support transition to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for dissemination of findings, manuscript production, and using pilot data to support competitive R00/R01 submissions and build collaborations for multi-site trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include presenting at national conferences (GSA, AAHPM, ASA), submitting manuscripts from pilot work, and mentor-supported grant submissions. The timeline should indicate production of pilot data and manuscripts to support R01 application.
